elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.4.1: "provided that AbbVie may make such an assignment without Harpoon's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor..." — AbbVie (Customer) retains the no-consent affiliate route; "Affiliate" is a defined term (1.16).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.4.1: AbbVie may assign without Harpoon's consent "to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates" — covers merger, stock sale and asset sale of the relevant business.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The general bar ("Without the prior written consent of the other Party ... neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign ...") is retained while the proviso was narrowed from "either Party ... without the other Party's consent" to "AbbVie ... without Harpoon's consent", so Harpoon now has no no-consent exception at all.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Existing, unedited words retained: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed", which now governs every Harpoon assignment because Harpoon's exception was removed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and Harpoon shall not assign this Agreement to a Competitor." Absolute (no consent override) and read with the void-assignment sentence ("Any attempted assignment ... in violation of this Section 13.4 shall be void").

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "A Change in Control of AbbVie shall not give Harpoon a termination right." "Change in Control" is the term already used in retained 13.2.1; Harpoon's remaining termination rights (12.2 breach, 12.4 insolvency) are untouched and are not CoC-triggered.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: As rendered, only AbbVie may assign to a successor without consent; Harpoon's successor assignment now falls under the general consent requirement, so the right is not mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: 13.4.1 contains no notice mechanic for a permitted successor assignment; 13.2.1's notice covers only a Change in Control of / Acquisition by Harpoon, not assignments generally.
The retained AbbVie affiliate exception ("without Harpoon's consent to its Affiliate") is a no-consent non-successor exception, which defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed".

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: the proviso was narrowed to AbbVie only (elements 1-3), the existing reasonableness standard was left verbatim (element 4), and two short insertions supply the Competitor bar and the no-CoC-termination confirmation (elements 5-6).

Targeting preferred rather than fallback is correct: the fallback would require deleting our own affiliate carve-out and adding a notice mechanic, i.e. a worse outcome for us; the fallback accordingly fails on three of its four elements as scored above.

Minimality holds. The only edits are (a) "either Party ... the other Party's" -> "AbbVie ... Harpoon's", which is necessary for element 3, (b) the Competitor bar, and (c) the one-sentence CoC confirmation. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or boilerplate was added, and the favourable retained sentences (affiliate performance responsibility, void-assignment, successor binding language, 13.2 Harpoon-side CoC regime, 12.3 AbbVie convenience termination) are untouched.

Intent preserved: no dangling cross-reference is created; "Change in Control" is the same term used in retained 13.2.1, and the retained sentence "With respect to an assignment to an Affiliate, the assigning Party shall remain responsible..." is not contradicted because Harpoon may still assign to an Affiliate with our consent.

Drafting note (not a blocker): confirm "Competitor" is a defined term in Article 1 and that it captures a competitor of AbbVie. It is capitalized in the inserted words but does not appear in the resolved definitions supplied (that list is incomplete - it also omits "Change in Control", which is plainly defined). If Article 1 does not define it, change to "a competitor of AbbVie or its Affiliates" so the prohibition is not left to an undefined or mis-directed trigger.

Optional tightening: element 6 was arguably already satisfied (Harpoon's only termination rights are 12.2 material breach and 12.4 insolvency, and 13.2 addresses only Harpoon-side Change in Control), so the added sentence is confirmatory; it is within the checklist and one sentence, so it does not breach minimality, but it can be dropped if the counterparty resists.
